Hi, just before you dash, Great Ormond Street Childrens Hospital. Have you heard of us? (YES) 

Brilliant! I'll keep this 30 seconds!
(We are actually ranked as top 3 for treating children with rare conditions, but) the reason we are here today is we're facing a massive issue with childhood cancer in the UK. We're losing a quarter of all the kids diagnosed, which I'm sure you can agree is way too much and something has to be done about it? (- YES) 

So what we're doing (and you may have seen it on TV) we're building the first ever state-of-the-art children's cancer centre. The idea being that research, treatment and recovery are all gonna be under one roof. There's also gonna be a school - for the kids to not miss out on education. The house bay is a brilliant place for parents to be able to stay on site, free of charge, with their children (where they need to be), but my favorite part is: on the rooftop there's gonna be a garden and a playground; you know, for the kids to be able to go outside, play in the sun, breathe fresh air, (it just brings that normality into their lives) which is so important, right? 

I'm glad you agree. But as you may have guessed, this is not free - the project costs 300 mil £, but the really good news is that we've actually already raised over half of it and started construction. We are planning to finish by 2027 but for that we need to find the rest, so what families are doing for us in about six weeks (start of september) is just sparing a couple of quid a week, less than a price of a coffee, for as long as they wish to help us. One of the main reasons why people choose this campaign specifically is because its restricted, so every penny donated only goes towards building this cancer centre, but most importantly getting those kids back home as quickly as we can. Do you reckon we could count on your support?

We are a local charity who takes care of kids at the end of their lives. Unfortunately since last year the demand for end of life care has risen by 47%. And the worst part is there's another 11000 estimated to still need our help, which is hard to believe, right?

	Law of Averages
Look at everything in terms of probability of it happening. Out of 100 people, if I smile and greet them enthusiastically 80 might engage. However if I was doing it without enthusiasm and without a smile only 40 would engage. 
The probability of success grows as the number of attempts grow. If I spoke to 10 people, I might not sell to anyone, but if I had spoken to 100, I could sell to 5

Get back to chapter one. Expand on it, talking about:

1) In terms of opportunities, the sales industry is rewarding for hard-workers. If you wish to work 80 hour weeks, you surely will get your recognition for it.
2) Sales offices use your dreams to manipulate you into working more. "Want to take a day off? I thought you really wanted to set the pace for your team, grow it, recruit more people, be promoted, ultimately get your own company?" another example "Only working till 17:30? I thought you really wanted that new phone"
3) "The harder you work now, the bigger the payback in the future"
1)	The three commandments: 1) Have a great Work ethic 2) Have a strong student mentality 3) Always have a positive attitude
2)	When interviewing, throw the interviewee on the back foot to make them feel inferior
3)	Ask for a physical copy of the CV and start writing on it. Assign it a number other than 1 to create a false impression that you have already interviewed other people today and to make the interviewee sell themselves.
